question_text: On which date was the historic declaration of independence broadcast by Major Ziaur Rahman on behalf of Bangabandhu from Kalurghat Radio Station?
explanation: Major Ziaur Rahman broadcast the declaration of independence on behalf of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman on 27 March 1971 from Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra in Kalurghat, Chittagong.

question_text: Where was the Mujibnagar provisional government of Bangladesh formally sworn in on 17 April 1971?
explanation: The Mujibnagar Government was formally sworn in on 17 April 1971 at Baidyanathtala in Meherpur district, later renamed Mujibnagar.

question_text: Who served as the Prime Minister of the provisional Mujibnagar Government during 1971?
explanation: Tajuddin Ahmad was the first Prime Minister of Bangladesh, leading the wartime provisional government during the 1971 Liberation War.

question_text: Who served as the Acting President of the Mujibnagar Government in the absence of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman?
explanation: Syed Nazrul Islam served as the Acting President while President Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was imprisoned in Pakistan.

question_text: How many military sectors was Bangladesh divided into during the 1971 Liberation War?
explanation: For operational efficiency, the Mukti Bahini divided Bangladesh into 11 military sectors under Commander-in-Chief General M. A. G. Osmani.

question_text: Which sector during the 1971 Liberation War had no regular sector commander and was operated as a naval commando sector?
explanation: Sector 10 comprised naval commandos and inland water transport; it had no permanent sector commander and operated under HQ commands directly.

question_text: Who was the Sector Commander of Sector 2 during the 1971 Liberation War until September 1971?
explanation: Major Khaled Mosharraf commanded Sector 2 (Dhaka, Comilla, Faridpur) until he was injured in late October 1971.

question_text: How many individuals were awarded the highest military gallantry award 'Bir Sreshtho' in Bangladesh?
explanation: Exactly 7 military and paramilitary personnel were awarded the Bir Sreshtho for unparalleled valor in the 1971 Liberation War.

question_text: Who was the only member of the Bangladesh Air Force to be awarded the Bir Sreshtho title?
explanation: Flight Lieutenant Matiur Rahman attempted to fly a T-33 trainer jet from Karachi to join the liberation movement and was awarded the Bir Sreshtho.

question_text: Which Bir Sreshtho recipient was an engine room artificer in the Pakistan Navy who joined Mukti Bahini naval forces?
explanation: Bir Sreshtho Mohammad Ruhul Amin served on the gunboat BNS Palash and embraced martyrdom on 10 December 1971 in Khulna.

question_text: On which date did the Pakistan Armed Forces officially sign the Instrument of Surrender at Dhaka Race Course (now Suhrawardy Udyan)?
explanation: Lieutenant-General A. A. K. Niazi signed the Instrument of Surrender to the joint Indo-Bangladeshi allied command on 16 December 1971.

question_text: Which Pakistani General signed the Instrument of Surrender on 16 December 1971 in Dhaka?
options: Lt. Gen. A. A. K. Niazi
correct_answer: Lt. Gen. A. A. K. Niazi
explanation: Lt. Gen. Amir Abdullah Khan Niazi surrendered with approximately 93,000 troops at the Dhaka Race Course.

question_text: Who represented the Indian and Bangladesh Allied Forces (Mitro Bahini) during the signing of the Instrument of Surrender on 16 December 1971?
options: Lt. Gen. J. F. R. Jacob
explanation: Lt. Gen. Jagjit Singh Aurora, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Eastern Command, accepted the surrender of Pakistani forces.

question_text: What was the codename of the brutal military operation launched by the Pakistan military on the night of 25 March 1971?
explanation: Operation Searchlight was launched on the night of 25 March 1971 targeting Bengali civilians, students, and intellectuals.

question_text: What was the codename of the major naval commando sabotage operation carried out by Mukti Bahini in August 1971?
explanation: Operation Jackpot was a coordinated naval commando strike carried out simultaneously at Chittagong, Mongla, Chandpur, and Narayanganj ports.

question_text: On which date is 'Martyred Intellectuals Day' (Shaheed Buddhijibi Dibosh) observed annually in Bangladesh?
explanation: 14 December commemorates the systematic execution of Bengali professors, doctors, writers, and journalists by Pakistani forces and collaborators in 1971.

question_text: On which date did Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman deliver his historic 7th March Speech at the Race Course Maidan?
explanation: Bangabandhu delivered his iconic speech on 7 March 1971, concluding with 'The struggle this time is the struggle for our emancipation; the struggle this time is the struggle for independence.'

question_text: In which year was Bangabandhu's Historic 7th March Speech registered by UNESCO as World Documentary Heritage in the Memory of the World Register?
explanation: UNESCO inscribed the historic speech on 30 October 2017 in the Memory of the World Register.

question_text: On which date was the historic Language Movement martyrs shot at in Dhaka by police in 1952?
explanation: Police opened fire on student demonstrators protesting for Bengali as a state language on 21 February 1952 near Dhaka Medical College.

question_text: In which year did UNESCO declare 21st February as International Mother Language Day?
explanation: UNESCO made the historic declaration on 17 November 1999, which has been observed globally since February 2000.

question_text: Who was the first martyr of the Language Movement on 21 February 1952?
explanation: Rafiq Uddin Ahmed was shot in the head near Dhaka Medical College and is recognized as the first martyr of the day.

question_text: Who designed the Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka?
explanation: Artist Hamidur Rahman, alongside sculptor Novera Ahmed, conceived and designed the Central Shaheed Minar in memory of the Language Movement.

question_text: Who was the architect of the National Martyrs' Memorial (Jatiya Smriti Soudho) located at Savar?
explanation: Architect Syed Mainul Hossain designed the Jatiya Smriti Soudho, composed of seven pairs of triangular wall prisms.

question_text: How many pairs of wall prisms make up the Jatiya Smriti Soudho at Savar, representing the seven stages of the liberation movement?
explanation: The 7 pairs of prisms symbolize the 1952 Language Movement, 1954 Elections, 1956 Constitution, 1962 Education Movement, 1966 Six Points, 1969 Uprising, and 1971 Liberation War.

question_text: Who wrote the famous patriotic song 'Amar Bhaier Rokte Rangano Ekushey February'?
explanation: The lyrics were composed by journalist and columnist Abdul Gaffar Choudhury in 1952.

question_text: Who composed the iconic, enduring musical tune of 'Amar Bhaier Rokte Rangano Ekushey February'?
explanation: Martyred composer Altaf Mahmud composed the famous melody in 1969, which is sung to this day.

question_text: Who was the foreign citizen who organized the historic 'Concert for Bangladesh' at Madison Square Garden in New York on 1 August 1971?
options: George Harrison and Pandit Ravi Shankar
correct_answer: George Harrison and Pandit Ravi Shankar
explanation: Ex-Beatle George Harrison and sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar organized the two benefit concerts raising awareness and relief funds for Bangladeshi refugees.

question_text: Which British photojournalist took iconic photographs of the 1971 atrocities and helped break the story internationally?
explanation: Daily Telegraph journalist Simon Dring evaded Pakistani military censorship in Dhaka and published the first eyewitness accounts of Operation Searchlight.

question_text: Which foreign journalist wrote the influential report titled 'Genocide' in The Sunday Times on 13 June 1971?
explanation: Pakistani journalist Anthony Mascarenhas fled to London to publish his explosive report, which shifted global opinion against the Pakistani regime.

question_text: Who was the only foreign national awarded the 'Bir Protik' gallantry award by the Government of Bangladesh?
explanation: Dutch-Australian William A. S. Ouderland, CEO of Bata Shoes in Tongi, aided Mukti Bahini freedom fighters and provided critical intelligence.

question_text: In which year was the historic 6-Point Movement presented by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in Lahore?
explanation: The 6-Point Charter for regional autonomy was placed by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman at a national conference of opposition parties in Lahore in February 1966.

question_text: In which historic trial was Sheikh Mujibur Rahman accused as the prime suspect by the Ayub Khan regime in 1968?
explanation: The case was officially titled 'State vs. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and others' in 1968, but was dropped following the 1969 mass uprising.

question_text: Sergeant Zahurul Haq, whose death sparked the 1969 Mass Uprising in East Pakistan, was killed while imprisoned in connection with which case?
explanation: Sergeant Zahurul Haq was shot dead on 15 February 1969 inside Dhaka Kurmitola Cantonment while in custody.

question_text: Which university student leader became a prominent martyr of the 1969 Mass Uprising on 20 January 1969 in Dhaka?
explanation: Shaheed Asad was shot by police near Dhaka Medical College on 20 January 1969; Asad Gate in Dhaka is named in his honor.

question_text: Which Rajshahi University proctor was martyred on 18 February 1969 while protecting student protesters from Pakistani military gunfire?
explanation: Dr. Mohammad Shamsuzzoha, Professor of Chemistry and Proctor of Rajshahi University, was the first university teacher killed in Pakistani custody in 1969.

question_text: How many administrative divisions are there currently in Bangladesh?
explanation: Bangladesh is divided into 8 administrative divisions: Dhaka, Chittagong, Rajshahi, Khulna, Barisal, Sylhet, Rangpur, and Mymensingh.

question_text: Which is the newest (8th) administrative division formed in Bangladesh?
explanation: Mymensingh Division was established as the 8th administrative division on 14 September 2015, carved out of Dhaka division.

question_text: How many administrative districts (Zilas) does Bangladesh have?
explanation: Bangladesh contains exactly 64 administrative districts.

question_text: Which is the largest district of Bangladesh by geographical land area?
explanation: Rangamati Hill District is the largest district by area, spanning approximately 6,116 square kilometers.

question_text: Which is the smallest administrative district in Bangladesh by land area?
explanation: Narayanganj is the smallest district by area, covering approximately 684.37 square kilometers.

question_text: What is the name of the longest natural sea beach in the world, located in southeastern Bangladesh?
explanation: Cox's Bazar features an unbroken natural sandy sea beach stretching approximately 120 kilometers (75 miles) along the Bay of Bengal.

question_text: Kuakata sea beach, renowned as 'Sagor Kannya' (Daughter of the Sea), is situated in which administrative district?
explanation: Kuakata is located in Kalapara Upazila of Patuakhali district and is famous for allowing panoramic views of both sunrise and sunset over the Bay of Bengal.

question_text: The Sundarbans, the world's largest contiguous mangrove forest, is shared between Bangladesh and which other country?
explanation: The Sundarbans spans approximately 10,000 square kilometers across southwestern Bangladesh (approx. 60%) and West Bengal, India (approx. 40%).

question_text: In which year was the Bangladesh section of the Sundarbans inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list?
explanation: UNESCO declared the Sundarbans of Bangladesh a World Heritage Site in 1997 for its unique biodiversity and mangrove ecosystem.

question_text: Which river enters Bangladesh from Tibet/India and is known as the Tsangpo in Tibet and Brahmaputra in Assam?
explanation: The Brahmaputra enters northern Bangladesh through Kurigram and takes the name Jamuna down to its confluence with the Padma at Goalando.

question_text: What is the mainstream name of the sacred Ganges river after entering the territory of Bangladesh?
explanation: The Ganges enters Bangladesh near Shibganj in Chapai Nawabganj district and is known thereafter as the Padma.

question_text: At which specific confluence point do the Padma and Jamuna rivers meet in Bangladesh?
explanation: The mighty Jamuna and Padma converge at Goalando Ghat in Rajbari district before flowing together toward Chandpur.

question_text: At which historic river port town do the combined waters of the Padma and Meghna merge before flowing into the Bay of Bengal?
explanation: The Padma and Meghna join together at Chandpur to form the Lower Meghna estuary emptying into the Bay of Bengal.

question_text: Which is the only coral-bearing island of Bangladesh, located in the southernmost part of the country?
explanation: St. Martin's Island is a small coral island situated in the northeastern Bay of Bengal, about 9 km south of the tip of Teknaf peninsula.

question_text: What is the officially recognized highest mountain peak in Bangladesh, located in Bandarban district?
explanation: Saka Haphong (also known as Mowdok Mual or Clan Moy) rises to approximately 1,052 meters (3,451 ft) on the Bangladesh-Myanmar border.

question_text: Kaptai Lake, the largest artificial man-made freshwater lake in Bangladesh, was created in 1962 by damming which river?
explanation: Kaptai Dam was constructed across the Karnafuli River for the Kaptai Hydroelectric Power Plant, submerging valley lands in Rangamati.

question_text: Which river in southeastern Bangladesh is internationally renowned as the only natural carp breeding habitat in tidal waters?
explanation: The Halda River in Chittagong is famous as the only tidal freshwater river where major carps (Rahu, Catla, Mrigal) spawn naturally.

question_text: Tanguar Haor, a globally recognized Ramsar wetland site, is located in which district of Bangladesh?
explanation: Tanguar Haor in Sunamganj district is a critical wetland ecosystem declared a Ramsar site in 2000, harboring hundreds of migratory bird species.

question_text: Which is the longest river entirely within the borders of Bangladesh?
explanation: The Surma-Meghna river system is considered the longest, though among purely internal tributaries the Surma river flows extensively through Sylhet basin.

question_text: What is the name of the narrow international border corridor between Bangladesh and India leased to Bangladesh in 2011?
explanation: The Tin Bigha Corridor connects the Dahagram-Angarpota enclave to mainland Patgram Upazila in Lalmonirhat.

question_text: Which line of latitude passes almost directly through the middle of Bangladesh?
explanation: The Tropic of Cancer (23° 26' N) passes across central Bangladesh, traversing districts like Chuadanga, Magura, Comilla, and Chittagong.

question_text: When did the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh officially come into effect?
explanation: The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 4 November 1972 and came into effect on Victory Day, 16 December 1972.

question_text: Who was the chairman of the 34-member Constitution Drafting Committee of Bangladesh in 1972?
explanation: Dr. Kamal Hossain, then Minister of Law, headed the committee that drafted the 1972 Constitution of Bangladesh.

question_text: How many fundamental principles of state policy are enshrined in the 1972 Constitution of Bangladesh?
explanation: The 4 fundamental state principles are Nationalism, Socialism, Democracy, and Secularism.

question_text: How many seats are there in the unicameral national parliament (Jatiya Sangsad) of Bangladesh, including reserved seats for women?
explanation: The Jatiya Sangsad comprises 300 general seats directly elected by single-member constituencies plus 50 reserved seats for women.

question_text: Who was the world-renowned American architect that designed the National Parliament Building (Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban) at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar?
explanation: Eminent architect Louis Kahn designed the iconic Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban, which was completed in 1982 and won the Aga Khan Award for Architecture.

question_text: Which ancient Buddhist vihara located in Naogaon district, Bangladesh, was built by Dharmapala of the Pala Empire and is a UNESCO World Heritage site?
explanation: Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur, built during the 8th century by Pala king Dharmapala, is among the largest Buddhist monastic complexes south of the Himalayas.

question_text: Mahasthangarh, the oldest urban archaeological site in Bangladesh situated in Bogura district, represents which ancient city?
explanation: Mahasthangarh is the ancient capital of Pundravardhana, dating back to at least the 3rd century BCE as evidenced by a Brahmi limestone inscription.

question_text: Who founded the independent Sultanate of Bengal in 1342, inaugurating the Ilyas Shahi dynasty?
explanation: Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah united the Bengal regions into 'Bangalah' in 1342 and took the title Shah-i-Bangalah.

question_text: The Sixty Dome Mosque (Shat Gombuj Masjid) in Bagerhat, a UNESCO World Heritage site, was founded in the 15th century by which Sufi saint-warrior?
explanation: Ulugh Khan Jahan Ali built the Khalifatabad settlement in Bagerhat, including the historic Sixty Dome Mosque with its 77 low domes.

question_text: Who was the last independent Nawab of Bengal who was defeated at the Battle of Plassey on 23 June 1757?
explanation: Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah was betrayed by his army chief Mir Jafar and defeated by Robert Clive's British East India Company troops at Plassey.

question_text: In which year did the historic Partition of Bengal occur under British Viceroy Lord Curzon, creating the province of Eastern Bengal and Assam?
explanation: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905 with Dhaka as the capital of Eastern Bengal and Assam; it was later annulled in 1911 due to intense protests.

question_text: In which year was the All-India Muslim League founded during an educational conference held in Dhaka?
explanation: The All-India Muslim League was established at Ahsan Manzil in Dhaka on 30 December 1906 under the leadership of Nawab Khwaja Salimullah.

question_text: Who is recognized as the pioneer of modern art in Bangladesh and founded the Government Institute of Arts (now Faculty of Fine Art, DU)?
explanation: Shilpacharya Zainul Abedin gained global renown for his 1943 Bengal Famine sketches and established the Dacca Art College in 1948.

question_text: Who was declared the National Poet of Bangladesh by the Government in 1972?
explanation: The 'Rebel Poet' (Bidrohi Kobi) Kazi Nazrul Islam was brought to Dhaka from Kolkata in 1972 and conferred the status of National Poet of Bangladesh.

question_text: Which poet is popularly revered in Bengali literature as 'Polli Kobi' (the Rural/Folk Poet) for works like 'Nakshi Kanthar Math'?
explanation: Jashimuddin celebrated rural Bengal's traditions, sorrows, and pastoral beauty in celebrated verse novels like Nakshi Kanthar Math (Field of the Embroidered Quilt).

question_text: Which traditional handloom muslin weave from Narayanganj was recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013?
explanation: Jamdani, an exquisite figured muslin textile produced along the Shitalakshya river basin, was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2013.

question_text: What is the traditional colorful procession brought out on the morning of Pohela Boishakh (Bengali New Year), recognized by UNESCO in 2016?
explanation: Mangal Shobhajatra, initiated by students of the Faculty of Fine Arts at Dhaka University in 1989, was inscribed by UNESCO in 2016.

question_text: In which year did the Bangladesh national cricket team play their inaugural official Test match, facing India at Bangabandhu National Stadium in Dhaka?
explanation: Bangladesh played their first Test match on 10 November 2000 against India, where Aminul Islam Bulbul scored a historic debut century (145).

question_text: In which year did Bangladesh win the ICC Trophy in Malaysia, securing their qualification for the 1999 ICC Cricket World Cup?
explanation: Bangladesh defeated Kenya in a rain-affected final in Kuala Lumpur on 13 April 1997 to lift the ICC Trophy under Akram Khan's captaincy.

question_text: What is the officially recognized National Game (Sport) of Bangladesh?
explanation: Kabaddi (locally known as Ha-du-du) is the constitutionally recognized national sport of Bangladesh.

question_text: Who was the first Bangladeshi all-rounder cricket player to be ranked ICC World No. 1 across all three formats simultaneously?
explanation: In January 2015, Shakib Al Hasan became the first cricketer in history to hold the number-one all-rounder spot across Test, ODI, and T20I simultaneously.

question_text: What is the total length of the road-rail deck of the landmark Padma Multipurpose Bridge inaugurated in June 2022?
explanation: The Padma Bridge has a main span length of 6.15 km across 41 steel truss spans connecting Mawa in Munshiganj with Janjira in Shariatpur.

question_text: What is the name of South Asia's first underwater expressway tunnel, constructed beneath the Karnafuli River in Chittagong?
explanation: The 3.32 km underwater tunnel connects Chittagong city with Anwara Upazila under the Karnafuli river bed.

question_text: The commercial operations of Bangladesh's first mass rapid transit metro line (MRT Line-6) commenced in December 2022 connecting which initial route?
explanation: The first phase of Dhaka Metro Rail (MRT Line-6) from Uttara North to Agargaon was opened to public service on 28 December 2022.

question_text: Bangladesh is constructing its first nuclear power plant at Rooppur in which district?
explanation: The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, featuring two VVER-1200 reactors with Russian Rosatom partnership, is located in Ishwardi Upazila of Pabna.

question_text: What is the name of the first geostationary communications satellite launched into orbit by Bangladesh on 11 May 2018?
explanation: Bangabandhu Satellite-1 was launched into orbital slot 119.1° East on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

question_text: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
explanation: The ohm (symbol: Ω) is the SI derived unit of electrical resistance named after German physicist Georg Simon Ohm.

question_text: Which chemical element has the highest thermal conductivity and the highest electrical conductivity of any metal at standard temperature?
explanation: Silver (Ag) possesses the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of all known pure metals, though copper is more commonly used due to cost.

question_text: What fundamental constant represents the speed of light in a vacuum, denoted as 'c'?
explanation: The speed of light in vacuum is an exact universal physical constant: 299,792,458 m/s.

question_text: What type of subatomic particle is exchanged to mediate the electromagnetic force in quantum electrodynamics?
explanation: In the Standard Model, the gauge boson responsible for mediating electromagnetic interactions is the massless photon.

question_text: Which planet in our solar system has the highest surface temperature, despite not being the closest planet to the Sun?
explanation: Venus has a thick atmosphere rich in carbon dioxide creating a runaway greenhouse effect, keeping its surface temperature around 465°C (870°F).

question_text: What is the largest moon in the Solar System, which is larger than the planet Mercury?
explanation: Jupiter's moon Ganymede has a diameter of 5,268 km, making it larger than Mercury (4,879 km) and Pluto.

question_text: Which scientist was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921 specifically for his explanation of the photoelectric effect?
explanation: Einstein received the 1921 Nobel Prize 'for his services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect'.

question_text: What organelle is famously designated as the 'powerhouse of the eukaryotic cell' where cellular respiration generates ATP?
explanation: Mitochondria convert nutrients into adenosine triphosphate (ATP) through oxidative phosphorylation.

question_text: What is the primary gas constituent of planet Earth's atmosphere by percentage volume?
explanation: Earth's dry atmosphere is approximately 78.08% nitrogen, 20.95% oxygen, 0.93% argon, and trace amounts of other gases.

question_text: What is the name of the supermassive black hole located at the gravitational center of our Milky Way galaxy?
explanation: Sagittarius A* is a supermassive black hole with a mass approximately 4.15 million times that of our Sun.

question_text: Who developed the world's first successful polio vaccine, using an inactivated virus in 1953?
explanation: Dr. Jonas Salk developed the injectable inactivated polio vaccine (IPV) in 1953, choosing not to patent it so it could benefit humanity broadly.

question_text: What is the atomic number of Gold on the Periodic Table?
explanation: Gold has the chemical symbol Au (from Latin Aurum) and atomic number 79.

question_text: Which space telescope, launched on Christmas Day 2021, orbits the Sun-Earth L2 Lagrange point to observe deep infrared cosmic history?
explanation: JWST was launched on 25 December 2021 aboard an Ariane 5 rocket and operates at the second Lagrange point (L2) 1.5 million km from Earth.

question_text: What rare chemical element has the lowest boiling point of all elements and remains liquid down to absolute zero at standard atmospheric pressure?
explanation: Helium boils at 4.22 Kelvin (-268.93°C) and requires pressures of at least 25 atmospheres to solidify even near absolute zero.

question_text: Which biological macromolecule carries hereditary genetic blueprints in humans and double-helix paired bases (A-T, G-C)?
explanation: DNA stores genetic instructions in sequences of nucleotide base pairs discovered in its helical structure by Watson, Crick, and Franklin in 1953.

question_text: In which year did the Roman Empire in the West officially fall when Emperor Romulus Augustulus was deposed by Odoacer?
explanation: The deposition of Romulus Augustulus in 476 CE is traditionally marked by historians as the collapse of the Western Roman Empire.

question_text: In which year was the Magna Carta signed by King John of England at Runnymede, establishing that the king was subject to the law?
explanation: The Great Charter (Magna Carta) was granted by King John on 15 June 1215 under pressure from English barons.

question_text: The fall of which historic imperial capital in 1453 marked the end of the Byzantine Empire and the rise of Ottoman dominance?
explanation: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II conquered Constantinople on 29 May 1453, bringing an end to the 1,100-year-old Byzantine Empire.

question_text: Which naval battle in 1588 saw the English fleet defeat King Philip II's massive Spanish fleet?
explanation: The Spanish Armada sent by Philip II to overthrow Elizabeth I was scattered and wrecked by English fire ships and North Sea storms in 1588.

question_text: What year did the French Revolution officially begin with the storming of the Bastille prison in Paris?
explanation: The storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789 is celebrated as the dawn of the French Revolution and is France's National Day.

question_text: Who was the military leader that crowned himself Emperor of France in 1804 and was finally defeated at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815?
explanation: Napoleon conquered most of continental Europe before his final defeat at Waterloo on 18 June 1815 by Wellington and Blücher.

question_text: Which major conflict between 1914 and 1918 ended with the signing of the Treaty of Versailles?
explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919, officially ending the state of war between Germany and the Allied Powers.

question_text: On which date was the attack on Pearl Harbor carried out by the Imperial Japanese Navy, bringing the US into World War II?
explanation: The surprise military strike on the US naval base at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii occurred on the morning of Sunday, 7 December 1941.

question_text: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall, symbolizing the imminent collapse of the Soviet Eastern Bloc?
explanation: The Berlin Wall, which had divided the city since 1961, was opened on 9 November 1989 amid peaceful democratic revolutions.

question_text: Which ancient civilization built the monumental complex of Machu Picchu high in the Andes mountains of Peru?
explanation: Machu Picchu was built as an estate for the Inca emperor Pachacuti in the mid-15th century and abandoned around the Spanish conquest.

question_text: What is the capital city of Canada?
explanation: Ottawa in Ontario was chosen as the permanent capital of the Province of Canada by Queen Victoria in 1857.

question_text: What is the largest country in the world by total land area?
explanation: Russia spans 17.1 million square kilometers across Eastern Europe and Northern Asia, covering over one-eighth of Earth's inhabited land area.

question_text: Which river is widely recognized as the longest river in the world, traversing northeastern Africa?
explanation: The Nile flows approximately 6,650 kilometers (4,130 miles) northward through 11 African nations into the Mediterranean Sea.

question_text: Which desert is the largest hot desert on Earth, covering over 9 million square kilometers across North Africa?
explanation: The Sahara covers most of North Africa, comparable in size to the entire land area of China or the United States.

question_text: What strait separates the continent of Europe from Africa, connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Atlantic Ocean?
explanation: The Strait of Gibraltar is approximately 14.3 km wide at its narrowest point between Spain/Gibraltar and Morocco.

question_text: What is the highest mountain peak on Earth above sea level, standing at 8,848.86 meters in the Himalayas?
explanation: Mount Everest (Chomolungma / Sagarmatha) lies on the border between Nepal and Tibet (China).

question_text: Which body of water contains the Mariana Trench, the deepest oceanic trench on Earth?
explanation: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific reaches a maximum depth of approximately 10,994 meters (36,070 ft).

question_text: What is the capital city of Australia?
explanation: Canberra was purpose-built as Australia's federal capital in 1913 as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

question_text: Which landlocked country in South America shares Lake Titicaca with Peru and has Sucre and La Paz as its capital centers?
explanation: Bolivia has Sucre as its constitutional capital and La Paz as its seat of government.

question_text: Which African country was formerly known as Abyssinia and was never colonized during the Scramble for Africa?
explanation: Ethiopia maintained its sovereignty throughout the colonial era, notably defeating Italian forces at the Battle of Adwa in 1896.

explanation: Tokyo is the officially recognized capital city of Japan.
